## 2026-08-14

### Features

- one-command first deployment alongside a live site (`ac1bede6`)
  scripts/first-deploy.sh brings this build up on its own compose project and its own port, so an existing site on the same server keeps serving throughout. Nothing is stopped, removed or overwritten; `down -v` on the project removes only this stack.

### Fixes

- catch a renamed database user before Prisma does (`426cf356`)
  Renaming POSTGRES_USER after the first run breaks the stack in a way the error does not explain. Postgres creates its user only when it initialises an empty data directory, so a later rename leaves the old database in place with nothing that can log in, and Prisma reports "P1000: Authentication failed ... credentials for `x` are not valid" — which reads like a wrong password rather than a user that was never created. Hit for real on a server while setting the admin password.
- let the stack come up without a Cloudflare tunnel (`32061094`)
  Two things blocked deploying this on a server that is already running something else.
- stop baking upgrade-insecure-requests into the build (`4857bf6e`)
  The site rendered as plain unstyled HTML in every browser while every server-side check passed. Root cause: upgrade-insecure-requests was written into the CSP at build time, from whether NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL began with https.

### Documentation

- add a CSS diagnostic and correct the stylesheet path (`96c1afe0`)
  The obvious check for "is the CSS there" gives a false negative: `grep _next/static/css` finds nothing on a healthy site. That path is webpack's; this app builds with Turbopack, which emits the stylesheet to /_next/static/chunks/<hash>.css. There is no .next/static/css/ directory and there should not be one.
- update changelog for the field service work (`ffc6e071`)
- correct the repository name after it was renamed (`550b726d`)
  The repository was created as `n8n` and is now `Vision-website`. The docs named the old one.
- changelog, backup, recovery and health check runbooks (`ade1f12b`)
  Four operational documents, each backed by a script so they are runnable rather than merely readable.
- DEPLOYMENT.md and PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md (`c3d9600f`)
  Complete build-and-deploy instructions for a clean Ubuntu server, and a folder-by-folder description of the architecture.

## 2026-08-12

### Features

- knowledge engine — article kinds, error codes, links (`250e7a43`)
  Knowledge is what this platform is actually for, so the content model stops being a blog. BlogPost is renamed KnowledgeArticle — a model holding error codes and troubleshooting notes shouldn't be called a post — via @@map, so it is a code-level rename with no table rename and no data movement.
- feature flags, content workflow, data quality (`ce299443`)
  Phase 2 foundations — the platform control the Knowledge Engine has to sit on.
- compatibility mapping, faceted catalogue, parts finder (`3bb3ea7e`)
  Session 3. Compatibility was a free-text string array, which cannot answer the question spare-parts buyers actually arrive with: "which parts fit my instrument?" It is now two real entities.
- search, mega menu, downloads centre, request quote (`ac590039`)
  Global search (/search) across instruments, spare parts, refurbished units, brands and Knowledge Center articles, grouped with per-group counts and filters. A plain GET form, so it works without JavaScript and results stay a shareable URL. Deliberately `contains` rather than full text: part numbers like 228-45103-91 are exactly what people paste in, and tsvector tokenisation would break them apart.
- seven homepage sections + announcement bar (`311e2d57`)
  Adds the sections the homepage was missing: company overview, featured products, brands grid, industries served, knowledge centre preview, testimonials and a contact band. All twelve sections stay CMS-driven — reorderable, hideable and editable from the homepage builder.
- light hero + project conventions (`e14a20ce`)
  Convert the homepage hero from the dark slate band to the white-first treatment used across the rest of the site. Product photography is mostly grey metal and reads poorly on a dark ground; the dark footer still anchors the page. Two-column layout with an image panel, accent colour reserved for the highlight word and the primary action.
- make Brand a first-class entity with hub pages (`2f2ced80`)
  Session 2 groundwork. brand was a free-text String on Product and RefurbishedInstrument, which meant no logos, no brand copy, no SEO, no brand page, and filters that depended on two people spelling "Agilent Technologies" the same way. Sessions 3 and 4 both need brand as a real thing to filter and attach documents to, so it is promoted now rather than after more data exists.

### Fixes

- decide cookie Secure from the request, not the build (`f6ca0a67`)
  The previous fix keyed the Secure flag off NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, which does not work the way it looks like it does. Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time, so that value freezes into the image: editing deploy/.env and restarting changes the container's environment and has no effect whatsoever on the flag. Measured directly - container env read back as http://192.168.1.5:8088 while the cookie still came out Secure=true, because the image had been built with an https site URL.
- keep sessions working on plain-http deployments (`81d0790d`)
  Three related auth defects, all invisible on localhost and all reproduced against the real compose stack served over a plain IP.
- don't send upgrade-insecure-requests on http deploys (`180bd6ec`)
  Found while debugging a LAN deployment where every page rendered completely unstyled even though curl showed the CSS returning 200 with valid compiled Tailwind.

### Chores

- declare the required Node version (`454afed5`)
  Building on the host with Node 20 hangs at "Creating an optimized production build" with no error. nanoid@6 requires ^22 || ^24 || >=26, and Prisma 7 wants ^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=24, but nothing in this project stated a requirement, so npm installed and ran without complaint and the failure surfaced as a silent stall much later.

## 2026-08-11

### Fixes

- fix Server Actions being rejected behind nginx (`43cbdc72`)
  Found by actually running the deploy/docker-compose.yml stack end to end for the first time (a real Docker daemon became available this session). Every form on the site failed with a 500 behind nginx:
- guarantee sharp's WASM fallback installs (`79d93617`)
  Different bug from the earlier sharp fixes, reported directly from a real server: "Unsupported CPU: Prebuilt binaries for linux-x64 require v2 microarchitecture". Confirmed straight from sharp's own shipped source (node_modules/sharp/dist/sharp.cjs) - it requires x86-64-v2 CPU features (SSE4.2 and similar) for its prebuilt native binary, and explicitly refuses to use it and falls back to a WebAssembly build when the host CPU doesn't have them, which is unrelated to and unaffected by the earlier lazy-loading fix (that changed when sharp loads, not what its binary requires).
- build succeeds with zero env config, fix start script re-run (`3aff98ce`)
  Found both while re-verifying the previous fix from a genuinely fresh checkout with no .env file at all (matching how the build was originally reported broken - before any database setup):
- lazy-load sharp, serve uploads dynamically (`cb92b4ad`)
  The previous fix's diagnosis was wrong: switching the build to Webpack didn't address the actual cause. Confirmed by reproducing the exact same crash ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'endsWith')" while collecting page data for /admin/blog) with Webpack too - it isn't Turbopack-specific at all, so that fix couldn't have worked. Reverted the build script back to the Turbopack default.

## 2026-08-10

### Features

- add Business Settings and wire it site-wide (`f1433935`)
  Build the Business Settings admin page (company details, phone/WhatsApp, address, social links, SEO defaults, logo, favicon) and thread it through every place those details were previously hardcoded or env-only: the header/footer wordmark now shows an uploaded logo (or the company name, still split-styled for the default), the footer gets a social links row, site metadata/OpenGraph/favicon come from Business Settings with the old env vars as a fallback, and every Call/WhatsApp button and the homepage's JSON-LD organization schema use the saved phone/WhatsApp number and address instead of a fixed value baked in at build time.
- add Media Library for browsing and deleting uploads (`ee8d3e5c`)
  List every file under public/uploads grouped with size and upload date, plus whether it's still referenced by a product, refurbished instrument, blog post, the homepage hero background, or the site logo/favicon - so an admin can tell what's safe to delete before doing it. Deleting an in-use file is still allowed (admin's call) but the confirmation warns about it explicitly. Also adds a standalone upload form for pre-loading images ahead of use.
- add Theme Customizer with site-wide color/font/button tokens (`238759c2`)
  Replace the ~50 files' worth of hardcoded blue-600/cyan-400 accent classes with CSS custom properties (--primary, --secondary, --btn-radius, --font-*) so the ThemeSettings an admin saves actually take effect everywhere, not just on a settings page. The root layout reads ThemeSettings on every request and overrides these variables inline, with a curated set of pre-loaded Google Fonts for the heading/body pickers (next/font requires static imports, so fonts are a fixed menu rather than free text) and a disable-animations toggle backed by a global transition-killing class.
- add About/Services/Contact/Header/Footer content editing (`95d00cdf`)
  Extend the admin CMS to the remaining site-wide content: About page facts, brands and why-us cards; Services page groups and services; Contact page copy; and the shared header nav / footer columns. All five now render dynamically from PageContent instead of hardcoded arrays, editable from a new "Pages & Menus" admin section, with the header nav links reused as the footer's Company column so there's a single source of truth for site nav.
- add homepage visual editor and CMS foundation (`560cb726`)
  Introduce a database-backed CMS layer so the homepage no longer needs a code change to edit: HomeSection/PageContent/SiteSettings/ThemeSettings models, Zod-validated content schemas with safe fallbacks, and an admin "Homepage Builder" with drag-and-drop reordering, visibility toggles, and per-section edit forms (Hero, Categories, Lifecycle, Why Us, CTA). The public homepage now renders dynamically from this data instead of hardcoded content arrays, preserving the existing visual design exactly.

## 2026-08-09

### Features

- security hardening pass (`3a70bddd`)
  Adds a Content-Security-Policy plus X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy headers at the app level (defense-in-depth alongside the existing Nginx headers). Adds in-memory rate limiting (documented as single-instance; a scaled deployment would need a shared store) to login (per-account and per-IP, to block both targeted brute force and spraying), account registration, the contact form and quote requests.
- SEO pass - sitemap, robots.txt, Open Graph and structured data (`fb7aebf6`)
  Adds a dynamic sitemap.xml covering every published product, spare part, refurbished instrument and blog post (hourly revalidation so it picks up admin changes between deploys), and robots.txt disallowing the private admin/engineer/portal sections. Root layout gets Open Graph and Twitter card defaults. Adds JSON-LD structured data: Organization on the homepage, Product on instrument/spare-part/ refurbished detail pages (price, availability, brand, SKU), and BlogPosting on knowledge center articles.
- add Docker Compose deployment (Nginx + Cloudflare Tunnel) (`1ab37782`)
  Multi-stage Dockerfile builds a trimmed Next.js standalone image (only traced production deps, no dev toolchain). docker-compose.yml wires up Postgres, a one-shot migrate+seed job, the app, Nginx as a reverse proxy, and cloudflared for a Cloudflare Tunnel - no ports are published to the host, so the tunnel is the only way in. Pins outputFileTracingRoot so the standalone build doesn't nest under an extra directory when built from within this monorepo checkout.
- add image upload pipeline for products, refurbished units and blog (`7e62990f`)
  Product photos, refurbished-instrument photos and blog cover images can now be uploaded from their admin forms instead of staying placeholders. Uploads are validated by decoding with sharp (rejecting anything that isn't a genuine JPEG/PNG/WebP regardless of the claimed content type), capped at 8MB, resized to a sane max dimension, and always re-encoded to WebP with metadata stripped before being written to a server- generated filename under public/uploads/. Product/spare-part cards, detail pages and the blog index/detail pages now render the real image when one exists, falling back to the existing placeholder otherwise.

### Documentation

- write full project documentation (`c721e0c0`)
  Replaces the create-next-app boilerplate README with real documentation: tech stack, the three-role feature set, a diagram of the quote-to-order and service-request-to-AMC/CMC workflows, project structure, local setup, environment variables, scripts, database/ seeding notes, image upload pipeline, security measures and SEO coverage, with a pointer to deploy/README.md for the Docker Compose walkthrough.

## 2026-08-06

### Features

- connect service requests and AMC/CMC contracts end-to-end (`cbae821c`)
  Admins can now manage all service requests (assign an engineer, which auto-advances OPEN to ASSIGNED; override status/priority) and create and manage AMC/CMC contracts (customer, instrument, visit allowance, contract value). Customers can link a new service request to one of their active contracts.
- build engineer dashboard (`edf35bc3`)
  Engineers can see active assigned jobs and priority/completion stats on their dashboard, move a job through assigned -> in progress -> completed, log visit reports (work performed, parts used), browse past job history, and edit their own profile. Job detail surfaces customer contact info and linked AMC/CMC contract visit counts.
- add admin engineers, reports and blog CMS (`e7b5b8d2`)
  Admins can now create engineer accounts (no self-registration path exists for staff roles) and activate/deactivate them, view a reports dashboard covering revenue, order/quote/service-request/AMC status breakdowns and top products by revenue, and manage Knowledge Base blog posts (create, edit, publish/unpublish, delete) that feed the public blog.
- add admin order/quote management and CRM (`d2f5776d`)
  Admin can now update order status and issue invoices, price and send quote requests, and convert accepted quotes into orders (carrying the source quote link). Customers get accept/decline actions on sent quotes from their portal.
- add admin panel core (products, categories, refurbished, inventory, customers) (`a350cd20`)
  Adds real CRUD across the catalog and operational data an admin needs day to day: products (instruments + spare parts) and categories, refurbished instruments, inventory (stock levels, low-stock alerts, stock movement ledger, suppliers), and customer accounts (list, detail with their full order/quote/service/AMC history, activate/deactivate). Admin dashboard ties it together with live cross-system stats.
- add customer portal and dashboard (`286d374c`)
  Adds the full customer-facing portal: dashboard with live stats (pending quotes, active orders, open tickets, next AMC expiry), orders (list + detail + repeat-order-to-cart), quotes, service requests (list + detail + new-request form backed by a real Server Action), AMC contracts, invoices, and an editable profile.

### Fixes

- commit package-lock.json for the vision-analytical subproject (`1801ad38`)
  The repo root's .gitignore blanket-excludes **/package-lock.json (correct for the pnpm-based n8n workspace), which was silently swallowing this subproject's npm lockfile too. Override it locally so installs stay reproducible, including in the Docker build coming up later.
